title: Sections and local equality after sheafification on a site
statement: Universe convention: let the objects of the site lie in Type u, its morphisms in Type w, and take set-valued presheaves in Type (max u w), so the set universe contains the site data and the plus construction. Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$, and let $\theta^2:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^\#$ be its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For every object $U$ and section $s\in\mathcal F^\#(U)$, there is a covering $(U_i\to U)_{i\in I}$ and sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ such that $s|_{U_i}=\theta^2(s_i)$ and, for every $i,j$, the pullbacks of $s_i$ and $s_j$ agree after a further covering of $U_i\times_UU_j$. Conversely, any such compatible local sections glue uniquely to a section of $\mathcal F^\#(U)$. In particular, if $p,q\in\mathcal F(U)$ have equal images in $\mathcal F^\#(U)$, then there is a covering $(U_i\to U)_{i\in I}$ on which $p|_{U_i}=q|_{U_i}$. This is Sites, Theorem Tag 00WB (theorem-plus) and Lemma Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification).

proof.text: Proved step: the universal sheafification unit is locally surjective, without a universe comparison. Let G be sheafify(F), eta its unit, and R the sheaf closure of the image subfunctor of eta inside G. Mathlib Subfunctor.sheafify_isSheaf makes R a sheaf. Factor F -> R through G using sheafifyLift. Composing the resulting lift with R -> G gives the identity by sheafify_hom_ext. Consequently every section of G belongs to R, so the image sieve of every section covers. This is the private Lean lemma unit_locally_surjective. The private helper is generalized to Category.{v} C; this argument does not require equal object and morphism universes.

For p and q with equal images under the unit, Mathlib Presheaf.isLocallyInjective_toSheafify′ supplies a covering equalizer sieve in the corrected universe. Apply Presheaf.equalizerSieve_mem and Precoverage.mem_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderComposition to extract a covering presieve on which their restrictions agree. This proves hlocal and the final conjunct.

Use local_representatives (image-sieve extraction and choice of preimages) to represent each sheaf section over a precoverage cover. For any overlap cone a >> f = b >> g, naturality of the unit and functoriality of restriction show that the two restricted representatives have equal images. Apply hlocal to those two sections and use Functor.map_comp_apply to identify their further restrictions with the desired composites. This proves the first conjunct including overlap compatibility.

Proved step: given locally compatible presheaf representatives, map them through the unit into the sheaf. Naturality carries each further-cover equality into equality after restriction in the sheaf. Separatedness on that cover proves compatibility on every overlap cone. The sheaf condition on the original covering then gives the unique amalgamation. This is the private Lean lemma local_descent. Apply local_descent to toSheafify with the sheaf property of presheafToSheaf.obj F. Combine all three conjuncts by And.intro.

lean.statement:
theorem sheafification_sections_local
    {C : Type u} [Category.{w} C]
    (J : Precoverage C) [J.HasIsos] [J.IsStableUnderComposition]
    [J.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [J.HasPullbacks]
    [HasWeakSheafify J.toGrothendieck (Type (max u w))]
    (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max u w)) :
    (∀ (U : C) (s : (sheafify J.toGrothendieck F).obj (op U)),
      ∃ (S : Presieve U) (x : ∀ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ U), S f → F.obj (op V)),
        S ∈ J U ∧
        (∀ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ U) (hf : S f),
          (sheafify J.toGrothendieck F).map f.op s =
            (toSheafify J.toGrothendieck F).app (op V) (x V f hf)) ∧
        (∀ (V W : C) (f : V ⟶ U) (g : W ⟶ U)
          (hf : S f) (hg : S g),
          ∀ (Z : C) (a : Z ⟶ V) (b : Z ⟶ W), a ≫ f = b ≫ g →
            ∃ (T : Presieve Z), T ∈ J Z ∧
              ∀ (Y : C) (h : Y ⟶ Z), T h →
                F.map (h ≫ a).op (x V f hf) = F.map (h ≫ b).op (x W g hg))) ∧
    (∀ (U : C) (S : Presieve U) (_ : S ∈ J U)
      (x : ∀ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ U), S f → F.obj (op V)),
      (∀ (V W : C) (f : V ⟶ U) (g : W ⟶ U)
        (hf : S f) (hg : S g),
        ∀ (Z : C) (a : Z ⟶ V) (b : Z ⟶ W), a ≫ f = b ≫ g →
          ∃ (T : Presieve Z), T ∈ J Z ∧
            ∀ (Y : C) (h : Y ⟶ Z), T h →
              F.map (h ≫ a).op (x V f hf) = F.map (h ≫ b).op (x W g hg)) →
      ∃! s : (sheafify J.toGrothendieck F).obj (op U),
        ∀ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ U) (hf : S f),
          (sheafify J.toGrothendieck F).map f.op s =
            (toSheafify J.toGrothendieck F).app (op V) (x V f hf)) ∧
    (∀ (U : C) (p q : F.obj (op U)),
      (toSheafify J.toGrothendieck F).app (op U) p =
        (toSheafify J.toGrothendieck F).app (op U) q →
      ∃ (S : Presieve U), S ∈ J U ∧
        ∀ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ U) (_ : S f),
          F.map f.op p = F.map f.op q)

STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the remaining local-injectivity assertion is false with the unrestricted independent universes u and w in the recorded Lean signature. For a sufficiently large complete atomless Boolean site, all Type w-valued sheaves are subterminal and their reflector exists as the sheaf closure of the support of a presheaf. The constant two-element presheaf reflects to the terminal sheaf, so its distinct sections have equal images and are nowhere locally equal on a nonzero object. The worker report gives the cardinality and support-reflector arguments. The previous double-plus dependencies only apply to Type (max u w), not to arbitrary Type w. No theorem of local injectivity in the unrestricted universes is added.
